outages.cause: Rolling and emergency blackouts after Russian attacks on energy infrastructure
outages.affected: Ukrenergo said that as of Thursday morning, Nov 19, consumers in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, and Sumy regions remained without power after Russian attacks over the previous 24 hours on generation facilities and electricity transmission and distribution systems. UNN, in a 9:31 a.m. EET Thursday report (1:31 a.m. CT), and Ukrinform, in a 12:13 p.m. EET Thursday report (4:13 a.m. CT), both citing Ukrenergo, said energy workers were working around the clock to restore electricity. Ukrenergo said that because of damage to energy equipment, emergency outages were currently being implemented in the Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. Ukrenergo said restrictions were being imposed in some regions through the end of the day: capacity-limitation schedules for industry, and hourly outage schedules from 0.5 to 3 groups for all consumer categories. No official national customer count was given. UNN also cited Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi as saying that Russians attacked energy infrastructure, civilian enterprises, and residential buildings overnight, that destruction was recorded in 12 regions, and that electricity substations were attacked in the Zhytomyr, Chernihiv, and Mykolaiv regions. UNN quoted Koretskyi as saying residential buildings in Zaporizhzhia, the Kharkiv region, the Cherkasy region, and the Donetsk region also came under attack, that eight people were wounded, and that one person was killed in the Chernihiv region; those casualty figures were not described as energy-sector casualties. Censor.NET, in a 12:50 p.m. EET Thursday report (4:50 a.m. CT) citing First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov at a briefing, likewise said consumers in the Dnipropetrovsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Mykolaiv, and Sumy regions had been left without electricity, and that emergency power outages were being implemented in the Sumy, Poltava, Kharkiv, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. It said a return to scheduled power cuts would be possible once the situation in the power grid stabilized, that most regions were also operating under hourly schedules ranging from half a shift to three shifts, and that power-restriction schedules were in effect for industrial facilities. It said a crew of power utility workers came under enemy attack twice in the Chernihiv region while performing their duties, with no casualties. RBC Ukraine, in an 11:04 a.m. EET Thursday report (3:04 a.m. CT) also citing Nekrasov, likewise listed those five regions as remaining without power as of the morning, but listed emergency outages only in the Kharkiv, Sumy, and Poltava regions; that shorter emergency-outage list differs from Ukrenergo's account and from Censor.NET's account of the same briefing, both of which also included Dnipropetrovsk. No official national customer count was given in those Thursday-morning reports. That Thursday-morning official status is later than Ukrenergo's Wednesday-evening notice that planned hourly power-outage schedules would be in effect around the clock on Thursday in parts of Ukraine. UNIAN, in a report updated at 9:44 p.m. EET Wednesday (1:44 p.m. CT) citing Ukrenergo, said that for all categories of consumers the Thursday schedules would range from 0.5 to 3 queues, corresponding to outages lasting from 2 to 12 hours, and that capacity-limitation schedules would apply to industry. UNN, in a 6:02 p.m. EET Wednesday report (10:02 a.m. CT) also citing Ukrenergo, likewise said one queue means four hours without electricity, so Thursday's outages may last from two to 12 hours. Focus, in a 12:43 a.m. EET Thursday report (4:43 p.m. CT Wednesday) citing Ukrenergo, said the electricity-supply situation remained most difficult in the Kharkiv, Sumy, Dnipropetrovsk, and Poltava regions, that in Kyiv on Thursday power would be cut for consumers in all 60 subgroups, and that in Kyiv Oblast, stabilization outages would average about six hours a day. UNIAN, citing Sumyoblenergo, said that in Sumy region on Thursday the total duration of outages, depending on the queue, would be from 8 to 12 hours. Those Wednesday-evening schedule reports did not give an official national customer count. In his evening address on Wednesday, reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 8:10 p.m. EET Wednesday (12:10 p.m. CT), President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said, following a briefing from Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal, that the electricity-supply situation was then most severe in the Kharkiv and Sumy regions and also difficult in the Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava regions, and that there had been strikes on Odesa and its surrounding region, as well as on the Mykolaiv and Zaporizhzhia regions. Ukraine's Energy Ministry, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 1:13 p.m. EET Wednesday (5:13 a.m. CT), said Russia had carried out more than 1,000 strikes on energy facilities since September and that the attacks had caused new power outages in the Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zhytomyr, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Sumy, Rivne, and Cherkasy regions as of Wednesday morning; it said emergency power cuts were then being implemented in the Sumy, Kharkiv, and Poltava regions, and that Zaporizhzhiaoblenergo reported that by Tuesday evening it and Ukrenergo had once again restored electricity to 390,700 consumers. Ukrenergo's Thursday-morning list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks did not include Odesa, Rivne, Donetsk, or Cherkasy; that is not an official restoration figure for earlier outages in those regions. Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne Regional Military Administration, said in a Telegram post reported by Ukrinform at 8:50 a.m. EET Wednesday (12:50 a.m. CT) that a Wednesday morning Russian attack had left more than 80 settlements in the north of Rivne region without power; no later official customer count or restoration notice for that Rivne outage was found. In Russian-occupied parts of the Donetsk region, occupation authorities reported that forced outages were continuing on Thursday (see the separate occupied Donetsk region row). No official national customer count was found.

outages.cause: Russian attacks on energy infrastructure, including new strikes on the morning of Nov 17 after earlier Nov 16 attacks on energy facilities in the region. Ukrenergo said consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power as of Thursday morning, Nov 19, and that emergency outages were being implemented there
outages.affected: Ukrenergo, as reported by UNN at 9:31 a.m. EET Thursday, Nov 19 (1:31 a.m. CT) and by Ukrinform at 12:13 p.m. EET Thursday (4:13 a.m. CT), said that as of Thursday morning consumers in Dnipropetrovsk region remained without power after Russian attacks over the previous 24 hours, and that emergency outages were currently being implemented in Dnipropetrovsk, along with the Sumy, Poltava, and Kharkiv regions, because of damage to energy equipment. Censor.NET, in a 12:50 p.m. EET Thursday report (4:50 a.m. CT) citing First Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov, likewise listed Dnipropetrovsk among the five regions with consumers left without electricity and among the regions under emergency outages. RBC Ukraine, in an 11:04 a.m. EET Thursday report (3:04 a.m. CT) also citing Nekrasov, likewise listed Dnipropetrovsk among the regions remaining without power as of the morning, but did not include it in the emergency-outage list in that report. No official customer count for the region was given in those Thursday-morning reports. That Thursday-morning official status is later than Wednesday reports that emergency outages were not being applied in the region. D1, in a noon EET Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing energy companies, had said that as of Wednesday morning emergency outages were not being applied in Dnipropetrovsk region and that stabilization (scheduled hourly) outages were in effect throughout the day by Ukrenergo order; Dnepr.info likewise said emergency outages had been cancelled on Wednesday. Dnipro.tv, in a 9:55 p.m. EET Wednesday report (1:55 p.m. CT) citing DTEK, said stabilization-outage schedules would be in effect in Dnipropetrovsk region on Thursday, Nov 19, for all six consumer groups throughout the day; that Thursday schedule is not a new official customer count. The latest official customer count found remains DTEK's Tuesday-morning figure. Suspilne, citing DTEK's Telegram page in an 11:18 a.m. EET Tuesday, Nov 17 report, said that after new large-scale Russian strikes on the region's energy infrastructure that morning, significant damage to energy facilities left 700,000 homes without power in Dnipro and the Dniprovskyi, Pavlohradskyi, Kamianskyi, and Samarivskyi districts. Censor.NET, also citing DTEK in an 11:22 a.m. Tuesday report, said 700,000 families were left without power in the region and likewise named those districts. No official restoration time was given. This is a later, separate wave of outages from Monday evening, Nov 16, when DTEK, in a Telegram statement reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 6:59 p.m. EET, said that after an attack on energy facilities in the region, the city of Dnipro was completely without power, and that some residents of the Dniprovskyi, Samarivskyi, and Kamianskyi districts were also without electricity. Dnipro Mayor Borys Filatov, in a Monday Telegram post reported by NV at 7:10 p.m. EET, said that after Russian attacks on the city, almost half of Dnipro was without electricity, and he called it the sixth blackout in two weeks. Zelenskyy, in the evening address reported by Interfax-Ukraine at 8:10 p.m. EET Wednesday (12:10 p.m. CT), said the situation was also difficult in Dnipropetrovsk region; he did not give a customer count for the region. No later official customer count or confirmation of full restoration after the Tuesday-morning 700,000-household figure was found.

outages.cause: Russian attack on DTEK energy facilities
outages.affected: 52,200 households without power, according to a Nov 16 statement by DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi. DTEK said a Russian attack on the morning of Nov 16 hit its energy facilities in the north of Odesa region, that 52,200 households were temporarily left without electricity, that specialists were inspecting surviving equipment in order to begin repairs as soon as possible, and that all work is being carried out under safety rules, including during air-raid alerts. DTEK also said the company's production site was damaged in the attack (windows blown out and ceilings and doors damaged) and that employees were not injured. No restoration time was given. This is a separate, later attack in the north of the region from DTEK's Nov 14 statement that a morning attack on one of its facilities there left almost 50,000 customers without power, and from the overnight Nov 15 DTEK attack that left 41,000 households without power in the Odesa region. In a separate Nov 17 statement, DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi said an energy facility in the south of the region was hit overnight Nov 17, that customers were re-energized where technically possible, and that 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power; that figure is for the southern Nov 17 attack and is not a later official remaining count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in a Nov 19 statement, said that over the last three days its crews had restored electricity to 128,000 families in 192 villages and towns of the region after new Russian attacks, and that restoration was continuing but was significantly complicated by frequent air-raid alerts. The same statement's introduction said crews had restored electricity to almost 130,000 families who had been left completely or partially without power. That is a three-day restoration total for the region; it is not a remaining customer count and is not a confirmation of full restoration for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that earlier weekly total also does not give a later official remaining figure for this morning Nov 16 outage. Ukrenergo's Thursday-morning list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks did not include Odesa; that is not an official restoration figure for this outage. A later Wednesday DTEK OEM item said crews would carry out urgent equipment repairs from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Thursday, Nov 19, with planned outages in parts of Izmail district and in Kyivskyi and Prymorskyi districts of Odesa and the suburbs; that is a planned Thursday repair outage and is not an official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage. A Thursday-morning recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page found no later official remaining customer count or restoration notice for this morning Nov 16 northern outage; the Nov 16 statement remained the latest official figure found for this specific outage.

The same statement's introduction said crews had restored electricity to almost 130,000 families who had been left completely or partially without power. That is a three-day restoration total for the region; it is not a remaining customer count and is not a confirmation of full restoration for this overnight Nov 15 outage. A Nov 16 DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi statement said that from Nov 9 to 15, crews restored power to 306,100 families in 637 villages and towns in the region; that weekly total covers Nov 9-15 and does not give a later official remaining figure for this overnight Nov 15 outage. outages.cause: Russian attack on energy facilities of another company in the south of Odesa region
outages.affected: No official customer count. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in a Nov 18 statement, said that toward evening on Nov 18 the enemy attacked energy facilities of another company in the south of Odesa region, and that outages were being recorded in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts. It said that as soon as it was safe, energy workers began inspecting equipment and clearing rubble, that the destruction was significant, and that repairs would take time. It did not give a customer count or a firm restoration time. Oleh Kiper, head of the Odesa Regional Military Administration, in a Telegram post reported by Ukrinform at 7:04 p.m. EET Wednesday (11:04 a.m. CT) and by Interfax-Ukraine at 7:16 p.m. EET Wednesday (11:16 a.m. CT), said the strikes caused power-supply disruptions in parts of the Bolhrad and Bilhorod-Dnistrovskyi districts, that no casualties had been reported, and that energy crews were assessing the damage and working to restore electricity. Suspilne, in a 6:16 p.m. EET Wednesday report (10:16 a.m. CT) citing DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi's Facebook page, likewise said part of customers in those two districts were left without electricity and that restoring the damaged facilities would take time. This is a later, separate event from DTEK's overnight Nov 15 outage that left 41,000 customers without power, from the morning Nov 16 northern outage that left 52,200 households without power, and from the southern Nov 17 DTEK attack after which 3,300 customers temporarily remained without power. DTEK Odeski Elektromerezhi, in a Nov 19 statement, said that over the last three days its crews had restored electricity to 128,000 families in 192 villages and towns of the region after new Russian attacks, and that restoration was continuing but was significantly complicated by frequent air-raid alerts. That is a three-day restoration total for the region; it is not a customer count for this Wednesday-evening southern attack and is not a confirmation of full restoration for this outage. Ukrenergo's Thursday-morning list of regions with consumers still without power due to attacks did not include Odesa; that is not an official restoration figure for this outage. A Thursday-morning recheck of DTEK OEM's official news page found no later official customer count or restoration notice for this Wednesday-evening southern outage.

outages.place: Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Khartsyzk, Torez, Debaltseve, and nearby districts
outages.cause: Occupation authorities said energy infrastructure was attacked on the nights of Nov 15 and Nov 16, causing an emergency in the regional power system. On Thursday, Nov 19, the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy said forced temporary outages were continuing because of emergency situations in the power system, damage to power networks as a result of UAV attacks, and a continuing shortage of available capacity and high load on operating equipment
outages.affected: Occupation authorities have not given a single independently confirmed total, and the latest official figures they issued still come from occupation sources. RIA Novosti, in a 1:16 p.m. Moscow time Thursday, Nov 19 report (4:16 a.m. CT) citing the press service of the occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, said forced temporary outages were continuing in a number of cities and municipal districts because of emergency situations in the power system, damage to power networks as a result of UAV attacks, and a continuing shortage of available capacity and high load on operating equipment. The ministry said the outages had affected 12 cities and municipalities of the region, including the Amvrosiivka municipal district, a significant part of whose territory remained without electricity. It said energy workers were continuing restoration work and that, as damage was repaired, the system stabilized, and technical possibility appeared, supply would be restored to consumers in stages. That Thursday update did not give a customer count and did not name all 12 cities and municipalities. The latest official remaining counts found remain those from Wednesday. News-donetsk.ru, in a 1:30 p.m. local Wednesday, Nov 18 report citing occupation government chairman Andrey Chertkov, said temporary outages were reintroduced Wednesday morning because of a shortage of available capacity and high load on the networks. It said partial outages affected Donetsk, Makiivka, Mariupol, Debaltseve, Yenakiieve, the Yasynuvata municipal district, Khartsyzk, Torez, the Shakhtarsk municipal district, and Horlivka, and that 125,000 residential subscribers remained without electricity and 228 boiler houses were de-energized. Later Wednesday, dnrnews.ru, in a 6:16 p.m. local Nov 18 report (9:16 a.m. CT) citing Chertkov, gave no new customer count; Chertkov said energy workers planned to reconnect all customers in the near future, which is not an official firm restoration time. Later Wednesday, RIA Novosti, in a 10:28 p.m. Moscow time Wednesday report (1:28 p.m. CT) citing occupation-appointed mayor Alexey Kulemzin, said electricity supply had been restored for more than 500 transformer substations in five districts of Donetsk; those figures are substation restorations in Donetsk city, not a remaining customer count, and they do not replace the 125,000-subscriber and 228-boiler-house figures. In a mid-afternoon Wednesday update, RIA Novosti, in a 5:20 p.m. Moscow time Wednesday report (8:20 a.m. CT) citing Kulemzin and Donetskenergo, said 33,302 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk because 226 transformer substations had been partially de-energized in the Petrovsky, Kievsky, Kuibyshevsky, and Kirovsky districts; that 33,302 figure is a Donetsk-city remaining count, not a later official regional remaining count. Earlier Wednesday, news-donetsk.ru, in an 8:09 a.m. local report citing Kulemzin and Donetskenergo, said 31,090 subscribers remained without electricity in Donetsk's Kalininsky, Proletarsky, and Voroshilovsky districts; that earlier city figure was superseded by later Wednesday updates. Earlier Tuesday, Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:31 p.m. local Nov 17 report citing the occupation energy ministry, said forced temporary outages were in effect in Donetsk, Horlivka, Yenakiieve, Mariupol, Makiivka, Torez, Khartsyzk, and Dokuchaievsk, as well as the Yasynuvata, Shakhtarsk, Telmanove, Amvrosiivka, and Volodarske municipal districts, without a customer count in that evening update. Donetsk Agency News (DAN), in an 8:30 p.m. local Nov 16 report, citing the occupation administration and Donetskenergo director Oleg Pavlyak, said 428,000 subscribers remained without electricity, a figure later superseded by the Wednesday remaining counts. A Thursday-morning recheck found no later official regional remaining customer count superseding the 125,000-subscriber and 228-boiler-house figures. These figures come from occupation authorities and were not independently confirmed in the sources reviewed.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The occupation Ministry of Coal and Energy, as reported by RIA Novosti at 1:16 p.m. Moscow time Thursday, Nov 19 (4:16 a.m. CT), said supply would be restored to consumers in stages as damage was repaired, the system stabilized, and technical possibility appeared. That is not an official firm restoration time.

outages.cause: Storms knocked down two major transmission towers and damaged a third at Wharminda, cutting ElectraNet transmission supply south and west of Whyalla
outages.affected: ABC News, in an article posted at 5:59 p.m. ACDT Thursday, Nov 19, and updated at 10:33 p.m. ACDT Thursday (6:03 a.m. CT), said more than 20,000 properties lost power on South Australia's Eyre Peninsula after a significant storm cell knocked over transmission towers in the region. It said about 24,000 properties on the peninsula remained without power at 9:30 p.m. ACDT Thursday (5:00 a.m. CT) after two major transmission towers were downed, and a third was damaged, at Wharminda, and that by 10:00 p.m. ACDT Thursday (5:30 a.m. CT) the number of properties impacted had fallen to about 14,500. ABC said that as of 7:00 p.m. ACDT Thursday (2:30 a.m. CT), almost 29,000 properties across the state were without electricity, about 24,000 of them on Eyre Peninsula, where supply was cut during lightning storms that afternoon, and that the same wild weather later started to hit Adelaide, causing more than 3,000 properties to lose power because of suspected storm-related faults on the distribution network. Earlier, ABC reported that as of 4:00 p.m. ACDT Thursday, SA Power Networks said extensive outages were impacting about 24,000 customers on Eyre Peninsula and western parts of South Australia. In a statement issued about 6:30 p.m. ACDT Thursday (2:00 a.m. CT), ElectraNet said the outage extended south and west of Whyalla, that power was unlikely to be restored in the immediate term, and that its first step was to safely assess the damage and then determine the quickest and safest way to restore services. The SA government warned that the main electricity transmission line to the Eyre Peninsula could take days to repair. After a meeting of SA cabinet's emergency management committee, Premier Peter Malinauskas said Minister Tom Koutsantonis had signed an emergency declaration authorizing him to instruct the Australian Energy Market Operator (AEMO) to seek spare generation, and that generators in and around Port Lincoln were going through a process of being energized. Malinauskas said such a step had the potential to restore electricity to the vast majority of those then without it, but that success was not guaranteed, and he said several schools in the region would stay closed the next day. Acting Police Commissioner Linda Williams said the state emergency centre had been activated at 6:00 p.m. ACDT Thursday (1:30 a.m. CT). Malinauskas said eight hospitals across Eyre Peninsula and Ceduna on the West Coast had been affected and were operating on generators. AEMO said that at that stage there was no broader impact to power system security and reliability in the National Electricity Market. Phone services on the peninsula were also reported to have been affected.
outages.etr: No official firm restoration time was given. The SA government warned that the transmission line could take days to repair. ElectraNet said power was unlikely to be restored in the immediate term. Premier Peter Malinauskas said energizing local generators had the potential to restore electricity to the vast majority of those then without it, but that success was not guaranteed.

outages.cause: Generation capacity deficit, with several thermoelectric units offline due to breakdowns and maintenance. UNE's Wednesday bulletin, published by Juventud Rebelde, said that unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance
outages.affected: UNE's Wednesday bulletin, published by Juventud Rebelde at 10:22 a.m. Cuba time Wednesday, Nov 18 (9:22 a.m. CT) and also summarized by CiberCuba at 7:58 a.m. Cuba time Wednesday (6:58 a.m. CT), remained the latest official national forecast found: if forecast conditions hold, 1,790 MW affected at the evening peak, with 1,040 MW available versus 2,800 MW of demand (a 1,760 MW deficit). At 6:00 a.m. Wednesday, the grid had 1,040 MW available versus 2,240 MW of demand, leaving 1,198 MW unserved, and UNE estimated 1,250 MW affected at midday. On Tuesday, service was affected by a generation-capacity deficit for all 24 hours and remained affected through the early morning; the maximum Tuesday affectation was 1,735 MW at 7:00 p.m. Tuesday. Tuesday solar photovoltaic output was 3,170 MWh, with a maximum of 493 MW at midday. The Wednesday bulletin said unit 1 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 2 of CTE Felton, and unit 6 of CTE Renté were in breakdown, and that unit 3 of CTE Santa Cruz, unit 5 of CTE Nuevitas, and unit 5 of CTE Renté were in maintenance. CiberCuba's transcript of the official parte said thermal generation limitations were 423 MW; Juventud Rebelde's reprint of the same bulletin said those limitations were 493 MW. The Wednesday bulletin no longer listed unit 8 of CTE Mariel among units in breakdown, a unit that had been listed in UNE's Tuesday bulletin. Official UNE and Juventud Rebelde sources did not report a total collapse of the national grid. A Thursday-morning recheck found no official Wednesday evening-peak actual from UNE and no Thursday UNE bulletin; Cubadebate's Unión Eléctrica tag still listed the Wednesday bulletin as its latest UNE dispatch. On Thursday, CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, said that at midnight Cuba time Thursday, Nov 19 (11:00 p.m. CT Wednesday) the utility reported 212 MW affected in Havana and that 77 distribution circuits were affected. At 3:08 a.m. Cuba time Thursday (2:08 a.m. CT), the utility reported 145 MW affected in 58 distribution circuits in Havana. CiberCuba's Nov 19 daily summary, still citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, later listed additional deficit outages on individual Havana circuits through at least 5:41 a.m. Cuba time Thursday (4:41 a.m. CT); those later circuit reports are provincial and are not a later official Havana total or a national UNE bulletin. CiberCuba's Nov 19 daily summary, citing the Empresa Eléctrica Villa Clara, also reported 198 MW affected in the province and said 133 interruptible circuits remained affected, and reported restorations on circuits 101 and 145 Cumbre in Placetas and on circuits 14 and 27. Those Villa Clara items were dated Thursday, Nov 19, but the summary did not give a specific clock time for the 198 MW or 133-circuit figures. Those figures are provincial and are not a later official national UNE peak figure. On Wednesday, CiberCuba, citing the Empresa Eléctrica de La Habana, had said that at 3:15 a.m. Cuba time Wednesday the utility reported 73 distribution circuits affected by a generation deficit, with 164 MW affected in the province; that Wednesday figure has been superseded by the Thursday Havana totals above. No official Wednesday evening-peak actual from UNE was found.

outages.place: Mayfair, Crosby, Brixton, Langlaagte, and nearby Johannesburg suburbs
outages.cause: A new trip of lines one and two at the Fordsburg Substation on Thursday, Nov 19. This is separate from the earlier Mayfair Substation fire and explosion that began Nov 8; City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena said Thursday that repairs at the Mayfair Substation following last week's fire and explosion have been completed
outages.affected: No official customer count from City Power for the Thursday outage. SABC News, in a 9:48 a.m. SAST Thursday, Nov 19 report (1:48 a.m. CT), said City Power reported another major electricity disruption after lines one and two at the Fordsburg Substation tripped, affecting several areas, including Mayfair, Crosby, Brixton, and Langlaagte. City Power spokesperson Isaac Mangena said technical teams were on site investigating the cause of the fault and working to restore supply. He clarified that the latest outage is at Fordsburg and not the Mayfair Substation, where repairs following last week's fire and explosion have been completed. Mangena said the latest disruption comes as the city continues to deal with more than 5,000 outage reports linked to storm damage, cable faults, theft, and vandalism; that is a citywide figure, not a customer count for the Fordsburg outage. No official restoration time was given for the Fordsburg outage. Mangena's Thursday statement that Mayfair Substation repairs have been completed is later than Nov 18 newspaper reports about remaining Mayfair-area customers. Daily Maverick, in a Nov 18 article, and The Citizen, in a 5:40 a.m. SAST Wednesday, Nov 18 report (9:40 p.m. CT Tuesday), both said that while the SABC, Netcare Garden City Hospital, and some industrial areas in Crown Mines had had power restored, more than 20,000 residents of Mayfair, Crown Mines, Homestead, Vrededorp, Pageview, Jan Hofmeyr, and Amalgam would have to wait for at least another week before their power came back on. That more-than-20,000-residents figure was reported by those newspapers and was not attributed to a City Power official count. Both reports quoted Mangena as saying that full power was restored after midnight on Sunday, that technicians were working on cable faults and on repairs at the Sentech tower, and that engineers were attending to further cable faults affecting customers in Mayfair West, Amalgam, Vrededorp, Homestead Park, Pageview, and Jan Hofmeyr, with remaining customers to be restored in phases once repairs were completed and the network was sufficiently stable, hoped to be completed by the end of the week. Those earlier reports were not accompanied by a later official City Power restoration notice specifically confirming that all remaining Mayfair-area cable-fault customers or Sentech had been restored. EWN, in a 3:43 a.m. SAST Thursday, Nov 19 report (7:43 p.m. CT Wednesday), quoted City Power acting chief executive officer Charles Tlouane, speaking at Wednesday's electricity imbizo in Braamfontein, as saying that outages at the Braamfontein substation and the long interruptions linked to the Mayfair substation have affected households, student accommodation, businesses, and institutions such as hospitals. He did not give a customer count for the Mayfair-area outage. There is no national Eskom load shedding; this is a localized Johannesburg distribution outage.

outages.cause: Drone attacks on power stations and other electricity infrastructure during the war between the Rapid Support Forces and the Sudanese Armed Forces
outages.affected: No official customer count. A United Nations report published Nov 17, issued in Geneva and posted on the UN in Sudan website, said that in just over two weeks between Oct 20 and Nov 4, 29 drone strikes, attributed to the Rapid Support Forces, hit electricity facilities and fuel stations across 11 states, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. It said the strikes had a devastating impact on civilians and essential services, causing power outages that disrupted health services including dialysis and surgical procedures, access to clean water, and food production. AFP, in a Nov 17 report on the same OHCHR findings, likewise said the intensification of drone strikes targeting power stations and fuel supplies had become a worrying trend, and quoted the report as saying that between Oct 20 and Nov 4 some 29 drone strikes attributed to the RSF hit electricity facilities and fuel stations, triggering widespread power blackouts and further fuel shortages affecting millions far from the conflict frontlines. That official humanitarian account is later than an Al Jazeera Nov 15 feature, which said the RSF has intensified attacks on power stations around Khartoum state over the past month, creating an energy crisis in the capital, and that there is no clear schedule for the resulting power cuts, which can last anywhere between six hours and a day. Al Jazeera said that between Oct 20 and Nov 2, 2026, there were at least 18 attacks on electricity infrastructure across at least nine states, leading to declining power generation capacity and fuel shortages. Citing The Associated Press, it said repeated drone attacks on power stations have seen electricity generation fall from about 4,400 megawatts before the war to about 1,100 MW today. Residents and a small-business owner in Port Sudan described prolonged, unreliable cuts, including outages lasting more than 24 hours. The UN resident and humanitarian coordinator, Denise Brown, was quoted warning that repeated strikes on power and fuel stations were disrupting dialysis, hospital births, and operations. No later official national customer count or restoration timetable was found. A Thursday-morning recheck found no later official national customer count or restoration timetable.
